## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-fascicle Eastern Jìn 東晉 translation of a short verse-discourse on the famous simile that, while the fragrance of flowers travels only with the wind, the fragrance of moral virtue (*sīla*) travels in all directions. The Chinese parallels are T99[1073], T100[12], [T117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0117) (Fǎxián), and *Ekottara-āgama* 23.5 (T125). The Pāli parallel is in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 54–55).

**Abstract**

T116 was produced during Zhú Tánwúlán's Yangdu translation period (381–395 CE), recorded in the frontmatter. The Indic source is presumed lost.
